original_forecast: When supported by the coupled brine/ice model, salt lowers the freezing equilibrium temperature and promotes melting that consumes latent energy. Cooling and melting can therefore occur together.

original_criteria.criterion: Compare both temperature and ice fraction before and after salt addition.
Include salt dissolution energy and any undissolved salt in the interpretation, rather than attributing every joule to freezing-point depression.

original_limits: This prediction requires brine/ice equilibrium coupled to dissolution and enthalpy; a missing coupling is a model-coverage result.

TC-008-C1.reason: Actual original thermometer observations and complete owned water phase inventories show simultaneous cooling and net melting after the unchanged salt dose.

TC-008-C2.reason: All salt dissolves to owned Na+/Cl-; independent common-reference Cp/fusion ledger explicitly includes endothermic dissolution and cold incoming solid salt, and closes without a compensating sink. Melting alone is not credited with every joule.
